name: responsive smoke — the same page on desktop and phone
note: The worked example for --passes. Run it as:
What it is FOR: not 'does the phone look nice' (that is taste, and taste is
yours). It is the narrow, machine-decidable question a second pass can
actually answer — did the same content arrive, and did anything break that
only breaks under a mobile UA, touch, or a narrow viewport. The cross-pass
report at the end is the output; a single pass's table is just half of it.
The `passes` field on an item scopes it. Use it for anything a responsive
layout is SUPPOSED to change — a check that is wrong by design on one pass
is worse than no check, because it trains you to skim past red.

items.claim: the page rendered under this pass at all
items.falsifiedBy: no snapshot captured, or the run never reached the end chapter

items.claim: the page has real text content, not an empty shell or an error page
items.falsifiedBy: the accessibility tree is empty, or shows only an error string

items.claim: no framework or server error page was served to this device
items.falsifiedBy: the screen says 404, 500, Application error, or Something went wrong

items.claim: nothing on screen tells the user to rotate or widen the window
items.falsifiedBy: copy like 'rotate your device' or 'best viewed on desktop' appears

items.claim: on a phone there is a way to navigate — a menu control or visible links
items.falsifiedBy: no menu/nav affordance anywhere in the tree on the phone pass
